summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (94/124)

data.turoyo: W bəṯr konəsli am mayanək w koḥərfi. Hanək kowən maye du tez, kəmmənne.
data.translation: Dann tropft das Wasser heraus und wird scharf, es wird "Scharfwasser" daraus, wie sie sagen.

rationale: First I Infectum example, koḥərfi with plural maye as subject; the leaching-water context provides an independent participant domain while retaining scharf werden.

summary: The inherited I Preterit Intransitive food example and new I Infectum water example share a change of quality with an affected inanimate subject. The III Preterit-wa knife quotation contrasts causation with inchoative I; its agent and anterior preparation are already documented.
koḥərfi at 94/124 has a plural water subject, whereas German uses singular Wasser. Retain the edition's wording and avoid deriving a separate technical meaning merely from Scharfwasser.
At 94/124, does maye du tez refer to taste, caustic strength, alkalinity or another quality? The supplied passage establishes scharfwerden but does not settle the chemical interpretation.
Scharfwerden also has water as subject in a dripping/leaching process. Whether the quality is taste or caustic/alkaline strength cannot be determined from the supplied verse alone.
